findings.title: No automated test that SQL expressions are rejected
findings.body: The PR adds a security gate that rejects QueryTypeSQL, but no unit test verifies the rejection, including when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled. Without a regression test, a future refactor could remove or weaken the gate and reintroduce the vulnerable SQL expression path.

findings.title: enableSqlExpressions is a no-op with misleading flag logic
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions computes enabled as the negation of FlagSqlExpressions and then returns false in both branches, so the feature flag has no effect. If the intent is to disable SQL expressions unconditionally, the conditional check is misleading and should be simplified; if the intent was to respect the flag, the logic is incorrect.

findings.title: User-facing error says SQL expressions are not implemented rather than disabled
findings.body: The rejected QueryTypeSQL path returns the error 'sqlExpressions is not implemented', but the feature is intentionally disabled for security reasons. This message can confuse users/operators, especially while the feature flag still exists.
